die_classes.note: 188 dies: 28 groups x 4 hold the 40 layers; 76 hold the Engram tables (202.8 GB), the embedding and the BF16 lm_head (4 dies run it)

definitions.mfu: model MACs of the EMITTED tokens per second / the class's peak MACs per second (lanes x m x clock x dies); 'array' = all 188 dies carrying the spec's blocks (as the spec is written), 'layer_dies' = the 112 dies that run layers
definitions.busy_fraction: a unit's issue time per wall time, mean over the layer dies (the model's issue: includes ROM-port or lane-quantisation stalls, replication and MTP positions)
definitions.mbu_rom_port: ROM weight bytes read per second / (provisioned read port x clock x 112 layer dies)
definitions.mbu_rom_macro: ROM weight bytes read per second / (macro sweep capacity 2.96 TB/s/mm2 x 289 mm2 x 188 dies)
definitions.mbu_hbm_kv: KV rows + index keys per second / (4.5 TB/s x 112 layer dies)
definitions.mbu_links: collective + hop payload bytes per second / (UCIe 4.2 TB/s + half the 2-die package's 1.19 TB/s SerDes) per layer die
definitions.critical_path_efficiency: exposed issue time of the units on the batch-1 critical path / the token time: how much of the token is spent doing work rather than waiting on depth, links and control

replicate_router.feasibility: replicate the BF16 router gate [384, 5120] on all 4 dies (3.9 MB/layer, +0.09% of the checkpoint's ROM): each die computes all 384 scores (53 cycles on the BF16 engine) and the router all-gather disappears; bit-identical (same FP32 dot per score)

replicate_a_proj.feasibility: replicate wq_a | wkv | index weights_proj on all 4 dies (+3 x 8.2 MB/layer, +0.2% ROM): q_a, kv and the index weights are local; the a all-gather disappears; bit-identical

rows_local_gather.feasibility: every die gathers all 512 selected compressed rows from its own HBM copy: the rows all-gather leaves the 8 index-source layers' path; costs 4x the compressed-KV capacity (1M users per die ~1,203 -> ~300)

direct_to_next_stage.feasibility: at the 29 group boundaries the partial sums cross the hop and the next group folds them (the one-shot engine's fold, fixed rank order: bit-identical); the residual copies ride ahead

cut_through_hops.feasibility: stage hops stream the residual behind hc_post (flit cut-through, credit per vector) instead of store-and-forward of 41 KB at 0.3 TB/s per neighbour

ring_placement_return.feasibility: fold the 29 stage modules into adjacent rack trays; the head dies also hold their embedding quarters, so the selected embedding row returns to S0 in one board hop instead of the generic mesh's 8

flat_one_shot.feasibility: each die gets board lanes to both dies of the partner package (the package's 90 lanes split per die; bytes stay overlapped): one board flight + fold per collective

oneshot_128_lanes.feasibility: requirement: the one-shot engine at LANES >= 128 (512 B/cycle) so a 20-KB all-reduce ingests within its producer's issue

unification.d_split_note: the pooled width 252,160 = 61.6 index keys/cycle x 4,096 MACs; the scan fits the pool only with the idx split-chain mode (d_split); without it 64 keys/cycle would need 262,144
unification.feasibility:
One block-dot pool for quantised weights AND the indexer (FP4 x FP4 is a mode of the FP8/FP4 block-dot:
    R-ARITH makes both a 32-block exact dot), one BF16 pool for BF16 weights, wo_a (FP8 codes dequantised at the
    lane input) AND attention (BF16 q/p x FP8 KV rows, the same dequantise-at-input mode).  Pool width = the
    larger of the two it replaces; the operand muxes (ROM read network | HBM key stream; ROM | KV staging) are
    charged 10% of the pooled engines' area (ASSUMED, no routed block).

nonlayer_right_size.head_dies_keep_stacks: 4 per head die for the drafter's per-user state at saturation (rack C10)
nonlayer_right_size.batch1_effect: none: the non-layer dies' engines never run layer work; KV lives only on layer dies
nonlayer_right_size.basis: busy fraction of a non-layer die's weight/attention/indexer/HC engines is 0 at every batch (they run no layer); the 4 lm_head dies need the BF16 engine, the vector unit and the one-shot engine; the Engram dies need only their per-bank gather slices and the assembler; the HBM stacks hold KV and index keys, which live on the layer dies (kv-lives-in-hbm), except the head dies' 4 stacks for the drafter (rack C10). Static saving on the table dies: HBM idle + logic leakage (0.10 W/mm2 of logic) x the removed ASAP7 engine area (ASSUMED scaling) + the SerDes they do not need (84 -> 2 lanes a package)

pareto.energy_basis: dynamic = the budget model's per-format MAC, ROM/HBM byte and link energies at the point's microbatch; clock gated per stage; static = the budget's per-die static 98.8 W (leakage, HBM idle, SerDes, UCIe idle), less the right-sizing saving on the 76 non-layer dies from 'L3+comm levers' on (ASSUMED scaling)

design_point.label: spec + chain ladder L1-3 + the adopted communication levers (replicate_a_proj, direct_to_next_stage, cut_through_hops, ring_placement_return, flat_one_shot, oneshot_128_lanes) + pooled engines + per-unit concurrency across microbatches; non-layer dies right-sized; MTP m = 2 at tau 5.0; operate at the 28-user pipeline fill

energy_with_static.basis:
J per emitted token WITH static power, ROM array vs HBM comparator, on one basis (spec agent request,
    2026-09-27): static = logic leakage + HBM stacks' traffic-independent power, charged on every die over the
    token; dynamic = the budget model's MAC / byte / link energies + the gated clock of the block area.

    * ROM die: the analytical N5 leakage (33.5 W, incl. ROM-array leakage) + 5 stacks x 2.8 W.
    * HBM die: logic leakage at the ROM die's logic density (N5 analytical: (33.5 W - ROM-array leakage) /
      525.6 mm2 of logic) x the comparator die's 618.3 mm2 of logic -- ASSUMED scaling -- + 5 stacks x 2.8 W.
    * 2.8 W/stack: technology.json power.memory_interface_idle_w_per_stack (DRAM standby + refresh + PHY and
      controller, band 1.2-6.4 W); the same term the ROM die's 14 W already is.
    * Sensitivity: technology.json's clocked-idle floor (50 W per device, applied as max(enumerated, floor)).
energy_with_static.note: rom_spec = the spec as written (188 uniform dies, spec engines); rom_design = the recommended point (pooled engines, adopted levers, right-sized non-layer dies); both machines at their own rates at each point; MTP on HBM at m = 2 as in the batch model
